claims.claim: The last-mile leg accounts for about 53% of total shipping costs (up from 41% in 2018), making it the most expensive part of the delivery chain.
claims.episode_span: The remaining distance to individual doorsteps can absorb the majority of the overall delivery expense, even though the physical distance is only a few kilometers.
claims.source_title: Last-Mile Delivery Statistics: The Complete Data Resource for 2026 (SmartRoutes)
claims.supporting_quote: Costs that once accounted for 41% of total shipping in 2018 now represent 53% in 2024, making the last mile the most expensive and operationally complex part of the last mile logistics chain.

claims.claim: Labor is the largest single component of last-mile delivery cost, at roughly 50-60% of the total.
claims.episode_span: Labor itself forms the largest single line item because the work cannot be fully automated while the driver must still locate doors, manage signatures, and handle exceptions.
claims.source_title: Last-Mile Delivery Statistics: The Complete Data Resource for 2026 (SmartRoutes)
claims.supporting_quote: Average consumer charge per delivery $8.08 Statista (2024) Labour as % of last-mile costs 50-60% Elite EXTRA (2023)

claims.claim: Delivered last-mile prices for a small parcel run to several dollars: typical urban deliveries cost around $10 per package, and rural ones far more.
claims.episode_span: Real delivered prices, however, are reported in the range of several dollars per small parcel.
claims.source_title: Last-Mile Delivery Statistics: The Complete Data Resource for 2026 (SmartRoutes)
claims.supporting_quote: Urban deliveries typically cost around $10 per package, while rural deliveries can reach $50 due to lower population density and longer travel distances.

claims.claim: Failed first delivery attempts add a discrete extra cost per parcel — industry estimates put the average cost of a failed delivery at just under $18.
claims.episode_span: Failed first attempts add another layer; when no one is home, the package returns to the depot or waits for a second attempt, doubling the labor and vehicle hours for that item.
claims.source_title: Last-Mile Delivery Statistics: The Complete Data Resource for 2026 (SmartRoutes)
claims.supporting_quote: Last mile delivery now accounts for 53% of total shipping costs Cost per failed delivery on average reaches just under $18

claims.claim: Consolidated delivery alternatives — parcel lockers, pickup points, and optimized networks — measurably cut last-mile trips and emissions.
claims.episode_span: Parcel lockers or neighborhood pickup points can raise the number of deliveries per vehicle stop from one to dozens, directly cutting the labor minutes per package.
claims.source_title: Last-Mile Delivery Statistics: The Complete Data Resource for 2026 (SmartRoutes)
claims.supporting_quote: Parcel lockers and pickup points in urban areas can cut CO2 emissions by up to two-thirds. Microhubs with zero-emission vehicles for final delivery achieve reductions of up to 93%. Consolidated deliveries using optimized networks can cut trips by 30%, lowering both costs and emissions.
